issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking increased compensation in a land acquisition reference must prove that the compensation awarded is inadequate with reliable evidence of comparable land values.
material_facts: The claimants sought further compensation for acquired land.
They did not examine witnesses to prove the prevailing market value of the acquired land or comparable nearby land.
They relied on mutation entries and on sale transactions mentioned in the Land Acquisition Officer’s award, but did not independently place those transactions in evidence.
issues.conclusion: The claimants did not establish a basis for increasing the compensation determined by the Tribunal.
issues.legal_principle: A reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act is an original proceeding, not an appeal. The claimant bears the burden of proving inadequacy by relevant and acceptable evidence, such as comparable sale transactions supported by evidence of the transaction, proximity, and similarity of the lands. Mutation entries are inadmissible for this purpose, and sale transactions mentioned in the Collector’s award cannot be relied on as evidence when they have not been independently proved before the Tribunal.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_reference: The matter is a reference proceeding to determine compensation for acquired land.
predicates.claimant_seeks_higher_compensation: The claimant asks for compensation above the amount already determined.
predicates.comparable_sales_not_proved: The claimant does not prove reliable comparable land sales through acceptable evidence.

issues.definition: When a claimant asks for higher compensation in a land acquisition reference but does not prove comparable sales with acceptable evidence, the compensation is not increased.

issues.legal_issue: A later compensation award that has not been admitted as additional evidence cannot support enhancement or require a remand.
material_facts: The claimants relied on a later Tribunal award concerning land acquired under the same notification.
That later award was not made part of the evidence in this appeal, and no application to admit it as additional evidence had been filed.
The later award was itself under challenge in the High Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court would not rely on the later award or remit the matter for reconsideration on its basis.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 41 Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, additional evidence must be received into the record before it can be considered. An award not forming part of the evidence cannot be relied upon; the fact that it is under challenge does not by itself justify remitting another matter for reconsideration.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.later_award_not_in_record: A later award is referred to but has not been admitted into the evidence record.
predicates.no_application_to_admit_additional_evide: No application is made to receive the later award as additional evidence.

issues.definition: In a compensation appeal, a later award outside the evidence record, where no application is made to admit it, cannot support enhancement or remand.

issues.legal_issue: A court exercising writ review cannot reappreciate evidence to substitute its own compensation assessment, and appellate interference is unwarranted where the Tribunal’s assessment rests on acceptable evidence and settled principles.
material_facts: The claimants challenged the Tribunal’s compensation award in a writ petition, and the High Court upheld it.
The Tribunal’s market-value determination was based on its appreciation of the evidence and its application of settled principles for determining compensation.
The claimants asked the Supreme Court to reassess the evidence and increase compensation.
issues.conclusion: The Tribunal’s compensation assessment was not disturbed.
issues.legal_principle: In proceedings under Article 226, the High Court does not reappreciate evidence and reach its own factual conclusion; it considers whether the Tribunal’s conclusion was warranted by the evidence and whether the correct legal principles were applied. A wholly unsustainable award may be remitted for reconsideration. In an appeal under Article 136, the Supreme Court likewise does not reappreciate evidence to substitute its own market-value finding where the Tribunal has relied on acceptable evidence and settled principles.

predicates.writ_review_of_compensation_award: The challenged Tribunal award is being reviewed in writ proceedings.
predicates.tribunal_assessment_supported_by_accepta: The Tribunal’s assessment rests on acceptable evidence and applies settled principles for determining compensation.

issues.definition: When a Tribunal’s compensation assessment is supported by acceptable evidence and settled principles, writ review does not disturb it by reappreciating the evidence.

issues.legal_issue: Claimants are entitled to the applicable enhanced solatium and interest on enhanced compensation under the land-acquisition amendment.
material_facts: The Tribunal had enhanced the compensation over the Collector’s award.
The claimants’ acquisition fell within the relevant amendment’s application, and possession of the acquired land had been taken.
The respondent accepted that the claimants were entitled to enhanced solatium and interest under the applicable amendment.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to additional solatium at 30 percent on the enhanced compensation and interest from the dates possession was taken, at the applicable rates and until payment or deposit of the additional compensation, whichever occurred earlier.
issues.legal_principle: Relying on Bhatinda Improvement Trust v. Balwant Singh & Ors., the Court held that the claimants were entitled to the additional solatium and interest provided by the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984, in respect of the enhanced compensation.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The compensation determined for the acquired land has been enhanced above the Collector’s award.
predicates.acquisition_falls_within_amended_benefit: The acquisition is within the class of acquisitions to which the applicable amended compensation benefits extend.

issues.definition: In a land acquisition compensation appeal, an award of enhanced compensation for an acquisition within the amended benefits entitles the claimant to additional solatium and interest.

issues.legal_issue: The additional amount under Section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act is unavailable where the acquisition notification and Collector’s award predate the provision’s applicable period.
material_facts: The acquisition notification was published before the Collector made the award.
Both events occurred before the period in which the additional amount under Section 23(1-A) applied to the acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were not entitled to the additional amount under Section 23(1-A).
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the temporal scope of Section 23(1-A) of the Land Acquisition Act and held that the additional amount was unavailable given the timing of the acquisition notification and the Collector’s award.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_case: The proceeding concerns compensation for acquired land.
predicates.notification_precedes_collector_award: The acquisition notification was issued before the Collector made the award.
predicates.both_events_precede_applicability_of_add: Both the notification and the Collector’s award occurred before the additional amount became applicable to the acquisition.

issues.definition: When an acquisition notification and the Collector’s award both precede the applicability of the additional amount, the claimant is not entitled to that amount.
